title: Does going first win the bargain?
hook: You make the first offer on a shrinking pie, with no deadline. How much can you keep?

knows: backward induction: in a one-shot take-it-or-leave-it offer the proposer can keep almost everything (lowball-offer-should-pass)
money later is worth less than money now
doesNotKnow: that when each delay shrinks the pie, the first proposer gets 1/(1 + δ), a small edge when delays are cheap

misconception: Whoever makes the first offer can grab most of the pie.
objective: The learner can explain, by stepping back from a deadline, that the responder's power is the value of proposing next round, so with a 10% shrink the first proposer keeps 1/(1 + 0.9) ≈ 52.6%, and that a costlier delay (50% shrink) raises the first proposer's share to 2/3.

claims.text: Each added round in front, the proposer must offer the responder 0.9 (at a 10% shrink) of what the responder would keep as next round's proposer, and keeps the rest. claims.text: With a 10% shrink per round, long games settle at 1 ÷ (1 + 0.9) = 52.6% for the first proposer; the learner's long game at 10% (400 rounds on the QA path; 50 rounds give 52.4%) is quoted from their own record.
claims.source: share(n) = (1 − (−δ)^n) / (1 + δ). Node: 50 rounds 0.5236, 51 rounds 0.5288, 400 rounds 0.5263; 1/1.9 = 0.5263. Matches the brief's check (company/domains/briefs/economics.markets.md #24). · Fact-check pass 23 2026-10-14: Own node: share(10%, 400) = 52.6%, 1/1.9 = 52.6%; closed form (1 - (-d)^n)/(1 + d) re-derived. The infinite-horizon value matches the finite limit (sup/inf argument re-derived: M <= 1 - dm, m >= 1 - dM give M = m = 1/(1 + d)). | v2: Demo.tsx share(0.1, 400) = 52.6%, share(0.1, 50) = 52.4% (builder's node run 2026-10-14). The reveal quotes the recorded long game at 10%, which is a required milestone (long-10). | FC pass 24 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Own node: recursion equals closed form (1 - (-d)^n)/(1 + d) for n = 1..400 at 10/30/50% (0 failures). share(0.1, 400) = 52.6%, share(0.1, 50) = 52.4%, 1/1.9 = 52.6%; every recordable 10% game (n = 50..400) lies in 52.4-52.9%, so 'close to 52.6%' holds on every path. Reveal quotes q = the longest recorded 10% game (records only grow; 1 round does not clear them). | v5 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14): reveal sentence reworded: "At 10%, your 400 rounds left the first proposer 52.6%, close to 1 ÷ (1 + 0.9): a small edge when waiting is cheap." (the "= 52.6%" after the formula was cut). | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. claims.text: With a 50% shrink a long game gives the first proposer 66.7% (30% shrink gives 58.8%); the costlier the delay, the bigger the first proposer's edge.
claims.source: 1/(1 + 0.5) = 0.6667; 1/(1 + 0.7) = 0.5882; 1/(1 + δ) falls as δ rises. Demo.tsx limit(). · Fact-check pass 23 2026-10-14: Own node: 1/(1 + 0.5) = 66.7% (reveal; 400 rounds also 66.7%), 1/(1 + 0.7) = 58.8% (stage dashed line at 30%); 1/(1 + d) falls as d rises. | v2: share(0.5, 400) = 66.7%, share(0.3, 400) = 58.8%. The reveal quotes the learner's recorded long game at another shrink (milestone long-other). | FC pass 24 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Own node: share(0.5, n) = 66.7% and share(0.3, n) = 58.8% for every n = 50..400; 1/1.5 = 66.7%, 1/1.7 = 58.8%; 1/(1 + d) falls as d rises. Reveal quotes the highest-shrink non-10% record (array sorted by shrink), either 58.8% or 66.7%, both above 52.6%, so 'the costlier the delay' holds on every path. | v5 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14): reveal sentence reworded: "At 50% shrink you saw 66.7%: costlier delay, bigger edge." The records row now reads "Long games (stand-in for no deadline): shrink 10% → 52.6% · 30% → 58.8% · 50% → 66.7%". | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own node: share(0.5, n) = 66.7% and share(0.3, n) = 58.8% for every n = 50..400; 1/1.5 = 66.7%, 1/1.7 = 58.8%; 1/(1 + δ) falls as δ rises. Reveal quotes the highest-shrink non-10% record (sorted), so a 30%-only learner reads 'At 30% shrink you saw 58.8%', also above 52.6%. claims.text: A game of 50 or more rounds stands in for no deadline: at a 10% shrink the first proposer's share is already within 0.3 points of the no-deadline 52.6% (the records row says 'Long games (stand-in for no deadline)').
claims.source: share(n) = 1 − δ·share(n − 1) converges to 1/(1 + δ) geometrically, error × δ each round; at δ = 0.9, 50 rounds give 52.4% and 51 give 52.9% (build note v1), 400 give 52.6%. Builder statement, not self-verified. | FC pass 26 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own node: |share(0.1, n) - 1/1.9| is largest at n = 50, 0.27 points (52.4% vs 52.6%), and shrinks by 0.9 each round (51: 52.9%, 400: 52.6%), so every recordable 10% game (n >= 50) is within 0.3 points. Records row string "Long games (stand-in for no deadline): ..." is on stage whenever a record exists, which the reveal requires.

recall.question: Two sides alternate offers with no deadline. Every rejected round, the money on the table shrinks a little (say 2%). Roughly how much does the side that offers first keep?
recall.why: The other side can wait one round and become the proposer, which is worth almost as much, so the first offer must give nearly half away: 1 ÷ (1 + 0.98) ≈ 50.5%.
